newsitem.title: ITALY: Dumped Italian ambassador says he was duped.
newsitem.headline: Dumped Italian ambassador says he was duped.

text.p: The Italian career diplomat who lost his job as the new ambassador to Albania 48 hours after his appointment said on Monday he had fallen into a trap in a newspaper interview published at the weekend.

Manfredo Incisa di Camerana, who was to have replaced controversial ambassador Paolo Foresti, had his nomination revoked on Sunday by the government after giving an interview to the newspaper La Repubblica the day before.
"I fell into a trap," Incisa was quoted as saying in the daily Corriere della Sera on Monday.
He did not elaborate, but the newspaper saw skulduggery behind the scenes at the Foreign Ministry.

It said the humiliating debacle suggested that Incisa had been the victim of a plot "set by elements in the ministry who do not look favourably on Foresti being replaced by a diplomat who sees things in a diametrically opposed manner."
The paper added that Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini had also been unhappy with the appointment of Incisa and had clashed with Prime Minister Romano Prodi over the issue.
Dini, attending a meeting of European Union foreign ministers in Luxembourg, angrily denied the report.
"We accept criticism but not invention. It is not the task of journalists to invent stories," he was quoted as saying by Italian the news agency Ansa.

Incisa, who had offered his resignation after La Repubblica quoted him as suggesting the ministry was going through a period of weakness and that Foresti had always been politically involved, kept to a more diplomatic line in the Corriere.
"I showed willing to take on the post, as I showed willing to give it up," he said on Monday.
"However, I have nothing to reproach myself for."
Incisa, who was formerly posted in Mozambique, said on Sunday that La Repubblica had quoted him out of context in an off-the record conversation.
The affair further embarrassed Italy after earlier controversy surrounding Foresti at a sensitive time with Albania preparing for elections later this month.
An Albanian newspaper had accused Foresti of bias in favour of embattled Albanian President Sali Berisha and trying to undermine the role of European mediator Franz Vranitzky.
Foresti, who will remain in Tirana until a replacement is found, has denied the charges.
Dini said the decision to accept the resignation of Foresti's successor and revoke the nomination was "a particular event involving an individual who has not shown himself to be up to the situation."

Italian opposition politicians said the controversy dealt yet another blow to the government's handling of the situation in Albania, which plunged into chaos earlier this year after the collapse of dubious savings schemes.
"(The government's action) continues to be marked by improvisation, amateurism and powerlessness," far-right National Alliance politician Maurizio Gasparri said.

Prodi defended the handling of the ambassadorial appointment on Sunday and said it did not affect Italy's role at the head of a multinational force which was deployed in Albania after rioting and looting in February and March.
